title: tier-2 shipped code: the client's tri-state boolean string parser against ParseBoolString (0x1424d8800)
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-casc/src/install.rs::parse_bool_string (now the body of parse_bool, which the .build.info row reader calls), built by cargo and called by crates/ow-casc/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the parse_bool_string entry.

FRAME: this is the harness's first exe-frame unit (`address.exe` + `base: 0x140000000`). The function loads its 16 spelling pointers from two tables in .rdata (0x143472f10 and 0x143472f50), and those table entries are absolute link-time addresses. Run in the v2b frame the first dereference faults at 0x143070584 (the exe address of the spelling "1"); with the image at its own base both the RIP-relative table load and the baked pointer resolve.

Oracle is ParseBoolString at exe 0x1424d8800, extent 0x1424d8800..0x1424d8916 (0x116 = 278 bytes through the ret), which is the declared coverageWindow. Signature: (const char *text, size_t len, u8 *flag) -> u8.

The client's read: fold a byte with `LEA EAX,[RCX-0x41] / CMP EAX,0x19 / LEA EDX,[RCX+0x20] / CMOVA` (A..Z to lowercase, nothing else); walk the caller's (text,len) against each spelling in order, ending a walk on a difference, on the spelling's NUL (both sides then hold NUL), or on the caller's length running out; the true table is 8 entries at 0x143472f10 (`1 on enable enabled yes y true t`) and the false table 8 at 0x143472f50 (`0 off disable disabled no n false f`). A match writes 1 (true table) or 0 (false table) to the flag and returns 1; when all 16 fail it returns 0 and never writes the flag.

Consequences the fixture pins: the length test precedes the first byte, so the empty string reports true; the caller's text must be a PREFIX of a spelling, so "tr", "enab" and "t�" match while "enablex" does not (the seventh byte is compared against the spelling's NUL) - the fixture caught exactly this in an early test comment; `on` is tried before `off`, so "o" is true and "of" false; nothing trims, so " true" and "true " match nothing and leave the flag at its 0xA5 sentinel.
Compared channels: the u8 return (AL; RAX's upper bits are contract-free, as its callers read only AL), the read-only text, and the 1-byte flag.

Coverage gate is 100% over the window's sites: both edges of the length test, the compare, the spelling-NUL test, the input-exhausted test, the 8-entry table walk (`CMP R9,0x40`) and the second table's duplicate of each.

acknowledgedGaps.what: a len larger than the text buffer
acknowledgedGaps.why: The client reads `len` bytes from the pointer it was given; a shorter buffer is a caller bug and would read past the arena. The probe rejects it and the fixture never builds one.

acknowledgedGaps.what: the tables' contents are image data, not tested values
acknowledgedGaps.why: The 16 spellings and their order are read from the image (both tables dumped qword by qword) and listed in the notes above; the unit proves the parser against them, not that the install's config uses each spelling.

knownEquivalentMutants.rationale: Line 226 is `if u32::from(c).wrapping_sub(0x41) <= 0x19 {`, the client's fold (A..=Z to lowercase). Flipping `<=` to `<` narrows the folded range to 0x41..=0x59 ('A'..'Y'), so exactly one byte changes behaviour: 0x5A ('Z') is folded to 'z' by the original and left alone by the mutant. The fold is applied to both sides of the walk and is length-preserving and per byte, and no spelling in either table holds 'z' or 'Z' (the 16 are 1 on enable enabled yes y true t / 0 off disable disabled no n false f), so an input 'Z' mismatches the same candidates either way. For every input the two programs agree on the return, the flag and the text. What would observe a difference: a spelling that holds 'z', or a caller that reads the folded byte itself.

The mutator's boundary rule on line 226 shifts the hex constant 0x41 to 0x40 (the 0x19 bound is followed by ` {`, which the rule does not touch), so the folded range becomes 0x40..=0x59 ('@'..'Y') instead of 0x41..=0x5A ('A'..'Z'). Two bytes change behaviour: 0x5A ('Z') is no longer folded to 'z', and 0x40 ('@') is now folded to '`'. The fold is applied to both sides of the walk and is length-preserving and per byte, and no spelling holds 'z', 'Z', '@' or '`' (the 16 are 1 on enable enabled yes y true t / 0 off disable disabled no n false f), so both bytes mismatch the same candidates either way and every spelling byte is unaffected. For every input the two programs agree on the return, the flag and the text. What would observe a difference: a spelling holding '@' or '`', or a caller that reads the folded byte itself. The sibling 'boundary +1' mutant (0x41 -> 0x42, which stops 'A' from folding) is not equivalent - the spellings hold 'a' - and it is left to be probed and killed.
